learning: If oscillation falls below 0.25 with the score at or above 153, derivative damping is the right lever at this geometry. If oscillation rises or line loss increases, kd is amplifying sensor noise, and the next step is to return kd to 0.3 and address yaw gain with kp.
notes: Iteration 6 geometry held exactly; the only change is kd 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the oval oscillation of 0.2505 seen at kp 3.5. Compare per track against iteration 6 (153.01).
rationale: Iteration 6 already raced this exact geometry (wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg) with kp 3.5, scoring 153.01. The Builder's proposal holds that geometry, so keeping the iteration 6 controller unchanged would repeat a known result and teach nothing. The one open problem in that race is oval steering_oscillation at 0.2505, just above the 0.25 caution level. Oscillation is the sum of changes in distance from the line between steps, so derivative action is the natural damper. I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.5 and keep kp 3.5 and ki 0.2, so kp/wheel_track is unchanged and the race isolates damping. Expected result: oval oscillation below 0.25 with progress near 0.73 and a score at or above 153. Risk: kd amplifies sensor noise, so if slalom line-loss events or s-bend max_error rise, kd is the likely cause. Geometry is held at iteration 6 values, and sensor weights, base_speed and line_loss mode are unchanged.
